title: Concrete strength under composition holdout

source.citation: Yeh, I. (1998). Concrete Compressive Strength. UCI Machine Learning Repository. DOI: 10.24432/C5PK67.
source.transformations: Converted Concrete_Data.xls to UTF-8 CSV, renamed columns, retained all 1030 rows and numerical values, added source row IDs and SHA-256 recipe keys from the seven supplied ingredient quantities. No deduplication, imputation, target transformation, or unit conversion.

independence.unit: Experimental unit should be an independently prepared/cured specimen or batch; original batch/specimen IDs are absent. The operational grouping proxy is the exact seven-component recipe, shared across curing ages.
independence.rationale: All observations with the same declared recipe stay together. This avoids testing the same recipe at another age, but does not establish independent experiments or resolve rounded near-identical recipes.

generalization.supports: Prediction for held-out exact concrete compositions within this source collection, conditional on supplied age and ingredients.
generalization.does_not_establish: Independent laboratory, publication, apparatus, chemistry-family or deployment transfer beyond the declared holdout.

limitations: Batch, laboratory, study and specimen identities are unavailable; grouping is a conservative composition proxy, not documented experimental independence.
Exact duplicate published records are retained; their experimental meaning is unknown. Equal-group metrics reduce between-recipe row-count weighting, but duplicates still affect within-recipe errors.
Exact composition holdout does not ensure chemical distance, multivariate extrapolation, or transfer to new cement sources.

accepted_warnings.duplicate_samples: Retain published observations because replicate/duplicate identities are not documented; composition grouping prevents these exact repeated records crossing partitions.
